content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert triggered: high 429 rate for customer 'Aurora Labs' in VPC 'aurora-vpc' (dedicated pool aurora-dedicated). 429s > threshold for 3m. Auto-page oncall. Alert: https://console.redwood/alerts/1790021111

paul_oncall: Acknowledged. tagging @nisha_sre and @omar_platform. Severity P1 until we confirm. Elaine (CSM) can you confirm impact from Aurora side?

nisha_sre: Looking at metrics: 429 spike originates from tenant t-aurora-7. 75% of requests hitting pool gateway return 429 RATE_LIMIT_POOL. No node restarts. CPU on pool hosts is high but not saturated. Queue length up ~3x.

omar_platform: Logs sample: 
```
[2026-03-15T22:05:03Z] tenant=t-aurora-7 POST /v1/chat -> 429 reason=RATE_LIMIT_POOL msg="pool tokens exhausted"
[2026-03-15T22:05:04Z] tenant=t-aurora-7 POST /v1/chat -> 429 reason=RATE_LIMIT_POOL
[2026-03-15T22:05:05Z] tenant=t-aurora-7 POST /v1/chat -> 200 status=ok duration=420ms
```
We see bursts followed by some successful reqs when queue drains. Could be a retry storm.

elaine_csm: On customer call: Aurora confirms they kicked off a large backfill job that started unexpectedly after a deploy. They say it started at ~22:00 and they paused it just now. They're asking for an emergency lift and want us to avoid a full outage.

paul_oncall: Two-track plan: 1) short emergency tenant-level lift (preferred, fastest) 2) immediate traffic shaping + routing fallback while lift is active. Kevin, can you prepare the lift and make sure billing/legal are notified?

kevin_infra: I can patch a tenant-level override for 90 minutes. Command: 
```bash
redwood-admin emergency-lift --tenant t-aurora-7 --pool aurora-dedicated --add-tokens-per-sec 2500 --ttl 90m --reason "customer backfill retry storm" --requester kevin_infra
```
I'll tag invoice/billing. Need approval from @omar_platform to proceed.

omar_platform: Approve. Also creating a routing rule to divert non-critical generation requests to model-quant-fallback to preserve capacity for latency-sensitive calls. Deploying as a canary at 25% first.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: routing-rule "aurora-divert-t7" -> model-quant-fallback. Canary 25% -> monitor 5m -> expand. rollout_id=roll-1790021111-a1

kevin_infra: Executing emergency-lift now... API returned success id=lift-1790021111. Audit entry created.
```
audit: user=kevin_infra action=emergency_lift target=t-aurora-7 delta_tokens_ps=2500 ttl=5400s id=lift-1790021111
```
Effect: pool token cap bumped immediately.

nisha_sre: After lift and canary routing: 429s dropped ~85% in 10m. Last 10min 429s ~40 (from ~900). Queue depth normalizing. Canary to 100% now.

omar_platform: Routing moved to 100%. model-quant-fallback taking ~60% of non-critical traffic. Latency on fallback higher but stable.

billing: Noted emergency lift id=lift-1790021111. Flagging for post-incident review for charge/credit.

security: Quick check: no auth anomalies, tenant isolation intact, no cross-tenant traffic. No security action required.

elaine_csm: Aurora reports their job is paused and they'll back off retries. They requested confirmation email with audit id and times. I'll file the ticket.

paul_oncall: Good. Plan: - Keep emergency-lift for 90m auto-revert - Keep routing rule until next sync with Aurora - Draft a short incident note for the customer with audit id - Postmortem assigned to @nisha_sre due 2026-03-18. Handing off to Nisha for writeup.

nisha_sre: I'll take postmortem. First-pass RCA: customer backfill caused an unexpected retry/burst pattern, our pool-level circuit tripped producing 429s. Remediations: 1) tenant-level dynamic backpressure detection 2) add SDK guidance to avoid tight retry loops 3) allow shared-burst elastic capacity for dedicated pools (product discussion).

paul_oncall: Thanks. Closing notes: Duration ~00:22 from alert to mitigation. No SLA breach reported. Keep channel open for 30m for any regressions.

incident-bot: Incident 1790021111 status -> MITIGATED. Resolution summary: tenant-level emergency lift + routing fallback. Postmortem owner: nisha_sre.

nisha_sre: I'll include the audit id lift-1790021111 and routing rollout roll-1790021111-a1 in the postmortem. Also will add a follow-up action to create an automated billing notification for emergency lifts.

paul_oncall: Great work everyone. Elaine, please send Aurora the confirmation with audit id and the brief blameless summary. :thumbsup:
